newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks says in talks to take over U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks says in talks to take over U.S. unit.

text.p: The truck unit of vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Monday it was in talks with General Motors about converting the U.S. group's 13 percent stake in Volvo Truck's North American company to preference shares.
After the deal Volvo would own all of the ordinary shares in the company, Volvo Truck spokesman Stefan Lorentzson said.
"We are negotiating about converting GM's shares to preference shares. This means that we will become the sole owner of ordinary shares in the North American company," Lorentzson told Reuters.
"The deal is entirely in line with what we said earlier about taking full control of our subsidiary," he said.
GM would still be represented on the board of the new company, he said. Volvo declined to comment on how much the deal would cost.
Volvo GM was set up in 1987 when GM wanted to end its heavy truck operations. At the time GM owned 24 percent of the company but since then the holding has been reduced to 13 percent.
